note: Every tunable number in the game. All values are first guesses. Nothing in the code should hard-code these.
gameNameNote: Working title. The final name is not chosen yet, so read the name from here wherever it appears.

cards.sharedNumbersNote: Each game the two cards share a random number of numbers from sharedNumbersBetweenPlayerCards up to that plus extraSharedNumbersMax (so 7 to 12).

pause.pausesNote: How many times the player can pause in one game. null means no limit; a number (for example 1) brings the limit back.

shout.levelNote: The microphone level is turned into 0 to 1 by mapping dbFloor (silence) to dbCeiling (very loud). Test your shout sets the player's level to calibrationFactor times their best shout, between minThreshold and maxThreshold.

check.checkNote: While the caller checks a claim: firstDelayMs is the wait before the first number; briskDelayMs is the wait for each number in the middle; the last buildNumbers numbers slow down (buildDelayMs, growing by buildGrowth each time); finalDelayMs is the wait before the very last number.

intro.note: Before the first number: the caller welcomes the player (a random line) while they look over their cards, then a 3, 2, 1 counts in the number circle. The 3, 2, 1 waits for the welcome line to finish being said (up to maxWelcomeWaitMs longer than welcomeSeconds).

credits.note: Closeness consolation: when a bot wins a stage, the player earns up to this share of the stage payout, scaled by how much of the pattern they had correctly marked.

animation.note: How things appear. Whole screens fade in calmly (the dark tense screens only fade; the bright ones also slide up a little). Small things such as the next-number card, the buttons and messages pop in with a little spring. All of it switches off when the phone's reduced-motion setting is on.

caller.note: How the animated caller behaves. He looks about every idleMinSeconds to idleMaxSeconds. Seasons turn on special looks around a date: month and day, daysEitherSide before and after. Add ?season=valentine to the address to preview one.

table.note: The regulars at the table. cardsPerRegular: how many cards each one plays. nearGoForFalseCall: a regular can only shout too soon when this close. botSitOutCalls: how long one sits out after a false call. A regular's reactionShare (in regulars.json) is how long they take to shout once they have it, as a share of one call, so slower speeds give the player more time. minReactionSeconds is the fastest anyone ever shouts.

race.note: Each night is planned as a story. 'arcs' lists the shapes a night can take for 1, 2 or 3 stages and how likely each is: W = a stage the player can win, L = a near miss where a regular gets there just ahead. A W stage is 'comfortable' (comfortableShare of the time: the best-placed regular finishes comfortableCalls after a sensible player) or 'close' (closeCalls after, a real race). A near miss has the regular finish nearMissCalls before. decoySpread: the other regulars finish this many calls after the rival (0 = the very same call, so they wait for the same number). decoyTieChance: in a close race, the chance one of them finishes on the player's own call. selfAdjust: the game remembers the last historyLength stages and tilts the shapes towards the targetWinRate. earliestCall stops anyone winning absurdly early. samples is how many random cards are tried to find the best fit.
